business.title: Discoverability Policy Design for Platform: Consider Customer Rating and Seller Competition
business.desc: Platforms commonly employ consumer rating systems to mitigate information asymmetry between sellers and consumers. Another tool that platforms often employ is paid discoverability services, which allow sellers to increase product visibility and attract more customers (e.g. front-page recommendations). While empirical studies have documented correlations between consumer ratings and platform discoverability outcomes, the underlying strategic interactions among platforms, sellers, and consumers remain underexplored. Using a three-party game theoretic model, we examine the strategic trade-offs inherent in the design of discoverability policies. First, we characterize the platform’s optimal discoverability policy when both consumer ratings and seller competition are taken into account. Second, our model sheds light on two puzzling phenomena: (1) Platform discoverability services may trigger adverse selection, thereby leading to market inefficiencies; (2) Some sellers may use ultra-low pricing to overcome consumers’ quality concerns, making price the determining factor for consumers to buy products while maintaining high consumer ratings. Our findings offer a nuanced theoretical lens through which platform operators and researchers can re-evaluate the interplay between consumer ratings and discoverability policies.

business.title: High-isolation 18-element multiband mMIMO antenna system for 5G smartphones using metallic side frames
business.desc: An 18-element multiband massive MIMO slot antenna system has been developed for 5G-enabled smartphones. The proposed design operates in LTE bands 42 (3.4–3.6 GHz), 43 (3.6–3.8 GHz), and 46 (5.15–5.925 GHz), thereby covering a wide range of global 5G frequency allocations. Each antenna element is excited through a U-shaped feedline coupled to an inverted T-shaped slot, enabling compact integration within the limited space of a smartphone chassis. To reduce mutual coupling between adjacent antenna elements, etched isolation slots are introduced on the metallic frame of the device. Both full-wave electromagnetic simulations and experimental measurements confirm the stable performance of the proposed system, achieving an envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) below 0.07 and a radiation efficiency exceeding 87% across all operating bands. In addition, the channel capacity analysis based on the Kronecker model shows that the maximum achievable throughput is 99.5 bps/Hz. The practical feasibility of the antenna system was confirmed with realistic smartphone conditions, such as user interaction, display module influence and battery placement. Furthermore, an information-theoretic approach that relates the electromagnetic coupling between the transmitting and receiving antenna surfaces to the mutual information between the two surfaces is introduced.

business.title: Cholesterol dysregulation contributes to hematopoietic failure in parn-mutant zebrafish with implications for dyskeratosis congenita
business.desc: Germline mutations in PARN cause dyskeratosis congenita (DC), an inherited bone marrow failure syndrome characterized by multilineage cytopenia and progression to myeloid disease. The mechanisms underlying this malignant transformation have not been fully elucidated. Here we show, using a loss-of-function CRISPR-Cas9 zebrafish parn mutant, hematopoietic stem and progenitor (HSPC) expansion and reduced mature hematopoietic cells across various lineages. Cholesterol biosynthesis was transcriptionally activated; a finding recapitulated in patient-derived iPSCs with PARN mutations. Inhibiting cholesterol biosynthesis rescued HSPC expansion and anemia in parn mutants. Concurrent myeloid differentiation therapy or Wnt inhibition reduced HSPCs to varying degrees. We further demonstrate a role for activated Erk signaling in impairing erythrocyte differentiation and show robust rescue with trametinib treatment. Overall, our findings uncover unrecognized roles for Parn in regulating cholesterol metabolism and Erk signaling and provide preclinical evidence for targeting these pathways to restore hematopoiesis in DC. Researchers show that abnormal cholesterol metabolism and Erk signalling disrupt blood formation in a zebrafish model of dyskeratosis congenita, identifying potential therapeutic targets for restoring healthy hematopoiesis in this patient population.

business.title: System of agentic AI for the discovery of metal-organic frameworks
business.desc: Generative models and machine learning promise accelerated material discovery in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 capture and water harvesting, but face substantial challenges in navigating vast chemical spaces while ensuring synthesizability. Here we present MOFGen, a system of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) comprising interconnected agents: a large language model that proposes MOF compositions, a diffusion model that generates crystal structures, quantum mechanical agents that optimize and filter candidates, and synthetic-feasibility agents guided by expert rules and machine learning. Trained on a broad set of experimentally reported MOFs and computational databases, MOFGen generated hundreds of thousands of MOF structures and synthesizable organic linkers. The uniqueness of our approach lies in its ability to generate large MOF structures with atomic precision, beyond the scale of conventional generative models limited to tens of atoms. This approach was validated through high-throughput experiments and the successful synthesis of four ‘AI-dreamt’ MOFs. An agentic AI system, MOFGen, is developed to accelerate the discovery of synthesizable metal–organic frameworks.

business.title: Genome-wide association study identifies a functional myostatin variant increasing lean mass in humans
business.desc: Muscle mass is central to physical function and metabolic health, but can decrease with disease, aging and weight loss interventions. As weight loss interventions become more widely used, agents that preserve or increase muscle mass are needed. To identify such therapeutic opportunities, we perform genome-wide association meta-analyses of arm, leg, trunk and total lean mass measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, a widely used method to estimate muscle mass. We identify 63 loci, including a rare missense variant in MSTN (p.Ile225Thr, rs143242500), which has the largest effect on leg lean mass (β = 0.28 SD [95% CI: 0.19, 0.37], P = 1.9 × 10-9). MSTN encodes myostatin, a negative regulator of skeletal muscle mass and a therapeutic target for muscle wasting disorders. Here, we identify a genome-wide significant association at MSTN in humans and characterize its functional consequences, providing genetic evidence that may inform the long-term systemic effects of myostatin inhibition. This large genome-wide meta-analysis identifies 63 genetic loci associated with lean mass, including a rare MSTN variant linked to greater muscle mass and strength, and provides insight into the long-term potential effects of myostatin inhibition.

business.title: Mid-infrared supercontinuum generation in fluoride fibers: a comparative study
business.desc: We present a comparative study of mid-infrared supercontinuum generation in fluoride optical fibers driven by a low-noise, Kerr-lens mode-locked Cr:​ZnS laser oscillator delivering ultrashort 35-fs pulses centered at 2300 nm. By investigating three commercial fluoride fibers with varying core geometries, numerical apertures, and chromatic dispersion profiles, we characterize how the magnitude of anomalous dispersion affects the dynamics of spectral broadening and the homogeneity of the supercontinuum. In fibers exhibiting high and steep anomalous dispersion, temporal pulse stretching triggers higher-order soliton fission, resulting in deeply modulated and fragmented spectra. However, combining a flat, near-zero anomalous dispersion profile with tighter spatial mode confinement supports efficient soliton dynamics and prevents early pulse walk-off. This results in the generation of a smooth, octave-spanning supercontinuum. Our experimental results, supported by numerical simulations based on the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation, demonstrate an ultrabroadband mid-infrared spectrum spanning 1600 nm to 5350 nm, with an average output power of 140 mW. These results highlight low-dispersion fluoride fibers pumped by femtosecond solid-state oscillators as a compact, robust platform for high-brightness, broadband mid-infrared light sources well-suited for molecular spectroscopy and trace-gas sensing.

business.title: ROME (INAFM2) expression is required for mouse parturition and postnatal survival
business.desc: We previously characterized the biochemical properties of the ROME protein and discovered its essential role in cancer cell metastasis and zebrafish development. To study the function of ROME in mammalian development and homeostasis, we created an inducible Rome knockout mouse model with tet-o-cre, M2-rtTA at the Rosa26 locus, and loxP sites inserted outside the 5’ and 3’ ends of the entire Rome gene. When Rome was deleted during embryogenesis by providing doxycycline in the feed to pregnant animals, phenotypically normal looking pups were born at the expected Mendelian ratio, but 86% of the pups with homozygote Rome deletion died within 72 h. Early postnatal mortality was primarily dependent on the genotype of the pregnant female as Rome deletion caused impaired parturition. In the F1 generation, Rome knockout mice surviving to adulthood exhibited unilateral or bilateral microphthalmia with 23% penetrance and a trend for the right eye being affected more frequently in the unilateral cases. These findings suggest that ROME expression during embryogenesis is critical for normal parturition and subsequent survival of pups in early postnatal life.

business.title: Gold prices could fall another 5% to $3,500 as Fed tightening fears grow - Razaqzada
business.desc: (Kitco News) - The gold market still has plenty of room to fall according to one market strategist as prices have been unable to hold critical support levels amid this week’s wave of selling pressure.In a note Thursday, Fawad Razaqzada, Market Analyst at FOREX.com, warned investors that gold prices could fall to $3,500 an ounce as expectations of interest rate hikes drive bond yields higher and support U.S. dollar strength.Razaqzada’s bearish warning comes as gold prices have dropped 5% so far this week, and his next downside target would represent another 5% decline from current prices. Spot gold last traded at $3,686.70 an ounce, down 1% on the day.“Rising global bond yields suggest markets are increasingly prepared for the Fed and other central banks to push interest rates higher in their efforts to bring inflation back towards target. Higher real yields are particularly damaging for non-yielding assets such as gold, and that remains the crux of the matter for the metal,” he said in his note.Gold’s decline has picked up momentum in recent days as Federal Reserve officials have reiterated their commitment to bringing inflation down to the 2% target. Although the central bank left interest rates unchanged last month, minutes from the meeting, published Wednesday, showed a clear tightening bias.Along with an expected rate hike in December, markets are also pricing in further tightening in January. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller also said Wednesday that the central bank may need “to shock people” with a 50-basis-point move next month.“Markets appear relatively comfortable pricing in 25bp hikes in December, January and again next summer, which is hardly an encouraging backdrop for gold,” said Razaqzada. “That pricing could come under scrutiny, but perhaps not until the release of November CPI on 10 December, when the impact of softer energy prices should become clearer. Until then, gold lacks an obvious catalyst for a sustained recovery.”Razaqzada said that one glimmer of hope for precious metals investors could come from the U.S. dollar index, as its rally back above 100 points has pushed it into overbought territory.“The dollar has given back a little ground today… But this looks more like a pause in the greenback's advance than any meaningful shift in the underlying trend, although even a deeper pullback would not come as a surprise given the extent of the dollar rally,” he said. “Put another way, gold's best hope of a bounce lies less in its own chart than in a pause in the dollar's rally. Until that happens, the path of least resistance remains to the downside.”On the upside, Razaqzada said that gold has a lot of work to do to repair the current technical damage. He said he would need to see a convincing push back above $4,140 before bulls return to the market.“That said, lots of overhead resistance levels lie ahead. Most importantly, the area between $3,837 to $3,870 is now likely to offer some resistance, having previously provided mild support,” he said. “Should gold get above that resistance zone, then things could get interesting again, particularly if there is a strong desire to push gold back above the summer low of $3,942 decisively.”Razaqzada said that he also expects silver prices to head lower, potentially falling to $40 an ounce.“From a technical analysis point of view, silver is still looking quite weak after failing to hold the support trend of its long-term wedge pattern,” he said. “Even if silver stages a rebound in the coming days, which would be a potentially bullish signal, further follow-up technical buying would be needed to suggest that the downtrend is over. Lots of broken levels could turn into overhead resistance if and when price retests those levels from underneath, including the $50 level.”See live precious metals prices for gold, silver, platinum and palladium — in USD, CAD and 12 more currencies.

technology.title: Genome-wide association study identifies a functional myostatin variant increasing lean mass in humans
technology.desc: Muscle mass is central to physical function and metabolic health, but can decrease with disease, aging and weight loss interventions. As weight loss interventions become more widely used, agents that preserve or increase muscle mass are needed. To identify such therapeutic opportunities, we perform genome-wide association meta-analyses of arm, leg, trunk and total lean mass measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, a widely used method to estimate muscle mass. We identify 63 loci, including a rare missense variant in MSTN (p.Ile225Thr, rs143242500), which has the largest effect on leg lean mass (β = 0.28 SD [95% CI: 0.19, 0.37], P = 1.9 × 10-9). MSTN encodes myostatin, a negative regulator of skeletal muscle mass and a therapeutic target for muscle wasting disorders. Here, we identify a genome-wide significant association at MSTN in humans and characterize its functional consequences, providing genetic evidence that may inform the long-term systemic effects of myostatin inhibition. This large genome-wide meta-analysis identifies 63 genetic loci associated with lean mass, including a rare MSTN variant linked to greater muscle mass and strength, and provides insight into the long-term potential effects of myostatin inhibition.
